plan-turnpike.hook: Fourteen km of smooth, wide curves climbing from the sea to 1,000 m.
moments: Pay the toll at the Odawara gate and start the long climb into the mountains.
Drive the flowing curves through cedar forest, with Sagami Bay opening up behind you.
Feel the air get colder and see snow on the roadside as you climb.
Park at the top at Taikanzan and look at the sports cars in the car park.
plan-turnpike.tip: Check @turn819 on X the same morning for ice and tyre rules. Drive it late morning, after the ice melts.

plan-taikanzan.hook: Mt Fuji rises white behind Lake Ashi, right from the car park.
moments: Step out of the car into air a few degrees below zero.
Stand at the rail and see Mt Fuji above Lake Ashi and the Hakone mountains.
Walk the car park and look at the sports cars that stop here on weekends.
Warm up with a hot drink in the rest area café.
plan-taikanzan.tip: Come before noon. The winter air is clearest in the morning, and clouds often cover Fuji after lunch.

plan-fun2drive.hook: You drive a real JDM car on Hakone mountain roads, a guide car in front.
moments: Pick your car in Sengokuhara: GT-R, Supra, RX-7 or Silvia.
Adjust the seat, feel the manual gear stick, and follow the guide car out.
Drive the Hakone mountain curves while the engine sound fills the cabin.
Stop with the guide and take photos of your car with the snowy mountains behind it.
plan-fun2drive.tip: Book 1 to 2 months ahead, ask for a manual car, and get the no-minimum-licence-years rule confirmed in writing.

plan-otome.hook: Mt Fuji fills the view as you drive down from Hakone to Gotemba.
moments: Pull in at the Otome Pass rest stop at the top of the pass.
Look out at Mt Fuji, big and white above the Gotemba plain.
Drive down slowly in low gear through the shaded, icy curves.
plan-otome.tip: Use low gear and do not brake hard. Shaded corners on the way down stay icy all day.

plan-oshino.hook: Water so clear you see five metres to the bottom of the pond.
moments: Walk the village lanes past thatched-roof houses with Mt Fuji above them.
Stand at Wakuike, the deepest pond, and look into the blue water and small cave.
See the water steam a little in the cold air. The springs stay about 11 to 14 °C.
Eat grilled mochi and a hot bowl of soba from the stalls.
plan-oshino.tip: Go before 10:00, before the tour buses. The paid Hannoki museum pond is not one of the real eight springs.

plan-chureito.hook: The red pagoda, Mt Fuji and the sunrise: the most famous photo of Japan.
moments: Climb the 398 stone steps in the dark with a phone light, breath steaming.
Find a spot on the viewing deck by 06:30, in the freezing morning air.
Watch the first sun turn the top of Mt Fuji pink behind the five-storey pagoda.
See the town of Fujiyoshida wake up below the hill.
plan-chureito.tip: Be on the deck by 06:30 for sunrise at 06:47. Wear shoes with grip; the steps can be icy.

plan-lake-kawaguchi.hook: Mt Fuji straight across the lake, turning orange at sunset.
moments: Park at Oishi Park on the quiet north shore of Lake Kawaguchi.
Walk to the water's edge and see Mt Fuji across the lake.
Watch the snow cap turn orange and then pink as the sun goes down.
Look for Fuji's reflection on the water if the wind is calm.
plan-lake-kawaguchi.tip: Arrive by 16:30 for sunset at about 16:55. The reflection is best when the lake has no wind.

plan-zao-onsen.hook: Milky, very acidic sulfur water in a snowy mountain village.
moments: Walk the steep village streets in the snow and smell the sulfur in the air.
Soak in a small old public bath like Kawarayu, Kamiyu or Shimoyu for a few hundred yen.
Feel the strong acid water (about pH 1.6) sting a little on the skin.
Eat Genghis Khan grilled lamb or Yamagata tama-konnyaku to warm up.
plan-zao-onsen.tip: Take off silver jewellery before the bath. Soak for short times; the acid water is strong.

plan-zao-ski.hook: Ski 10 km from the snow monsters at the top down to the village.
moments: Ride the ropeway up and see the frozen trees all around you.
Ski the long Juhyo course between snow monsters, about 10 km to the bottom.
Learn on the gentle, wide Uenodai slope right next to the village.
Stop for a hot lunch in a slope-side restaurant with snow on the windows.
plan-zao-ski.tip: Book an English private lesson for the beginner before the trip. Bring your own boots if over 28 cm.

plan-zao-juhyo.hook: Frozen trees shaped like giant white monsters, lit in colour at night.
moments: Ride the Zao Ropeway up through the dark forest to Jizo Sancho station at 1,661 m.
Step out into −10 °C and hear the snow crunch under your boots.
Walk among the snow monsters, lit in blue, green and purple.
Find the stone Jizo statue at the top, almost buried in snow.
Ride back down and go straight into a hot sulfur bath.
plan-zao-juhyo.tip: Light-up dates for 2027 come out in December. Last ropeway up is about 19:50. Cover your face; the wind is very cold.

plan-ryokan-zao.hook: Sulfur baths, kaiseki dinner and a yukata, next to the ropeway.
moments: Leave your bags, change into the yukata and go straight to the milky sulfur bath.
Eat a many-course kaiseki dinner in your yukata.
Walk to the other Takamiya inns in the village and try their baths for free.
Soak again late at night while snow falls outside.
plan-ryokan-zao.tip: If you go to the snow monster light-up, ask for the late dinner time. Ask for a private bath if you have tattoos.

plan-sendai-st.hook: Thick charcoal-grilled beef tongue, six shops in one row inside the station.
moments: Walk the 3rd floor Gyutan Street and pick a shop: Rikyu, Date no Gyutan or Kisuke.
Order the teishoku set, thick cut, with barley rice and oxtail soup.
Bite into the chewy, smoky tongue with a little green chili miso.
Buy a gyutan ekiben for the Hayabusa north. Pull the string and the box heats itself.
plan-sendai-st.tip: Ask for 厚切り (atsugiri, thick cut). Go before 18:00 or after 20:00 to skip the longest lines.

plan-matsushima.hook: About 260 small pine islands, and hot grilled oysters by the sea.
moments: Ride the Senseki Line 40 minutes from Sendai to Matsushima-Kaigan.
Cross the short bridges to Godaido, the small temple hall on its own rock.
Walk the long red Fukuura bridge to the island and look back at the bay.
Eat grilled oysters, hot and salty, in winter oyster season.
plan-matsushima.tip: Optional stop. Take the 50-minute island boat only if you have time; the bridges give good views for free.

plan-kanemori.hook: Red brick harbour warehouses from 1887, snow on the roofs at dusk.
moments: Walk along the small canal between the red brick warehouses as the lights come on.
Look in the shops of BAY Hakodate and Kanemori Yobutsukan.
Eat dinner and drink local beer in the Hakodate Beer Hall.
Walk the snowy harbour front with the bay dark beside you.
plan-kanemori.tip: Come at dusk, right after the lights come on, for the best photos of the snowy bricks.

plan-mt-hakodate.hook: City lights on a narrow strip of land between two black bays.
moments: Ride the big ropeway gondola up 334 m in a few minutes.
Stand on the top deck and watch the sun go down over the sea.
See the city lights come on, making the famous shape between the two bays.
Warm your hands in the indoor observation room after the cold wind.
plan-mt-hakodate.tip: Go up about 16:15 for sunset at 16:36. The road is closed to cars in winter, so take the ropeway.

plan-asaichi.hook: Catch a live squid yourself and eat it seconds later, still moving.
moments: Walk the morning market stalls past piles of crab, uni and ikura.
Catch a live squid with a rod at the Ekini Market squid pool.
Watch staff slice it on the spot. Eat it with soy and ginger while the legs still move.
Eat a small seafood bowl with ikura and uni in Donburi Yokocho.
plan-asaichi.tip: Come early morning when stalls are busy. If you ate breakfast, try the squid fishing and share one small bowl.
